newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat harvest more than 25 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat harvest more than 25 percent complete.

text.p: Harvesting of Texas wheat progressed during the week ended Sunday and was more than 25 percent complete, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
"High winds, heavy downpours and hail caused damage in numerous fields," the report said. "Despite the weather problems, crops made remarkably good progress."

Wheat was 26 percent harvested, against nine last week, 49 last year and 36 percent on average. The condition of the state's wheat crop improved and was rated four percent very poor, 10 poor, 30 fair, 46 good and 10 percent excellent.

Corn was 29 percent silked, against 48 percent last year and 47 on average. Fields were beginning to dent in the Rio Grande Valley and Coastal Bend areas. Corn condition improved and was rated 26 percent excellent, 61 good, 10 fair, three poor and nil very poor.
Sorghum was 26 percent headed versus 39 a year ago and 44 percent on average. Sorghum was rated 16 percent excellent, 46 good, 30 fair, 10 good and four excellent.
Sunflowers were 51 percent planted versus 56 a year ago and 65 on average. Cotton was 93 percent planted, versus 86 last year and 88 on average.
